newsitem.title: TURKEY: AKBANK TO ADD 17 TRLN LIRA CAPITAL GAIN TO CAPITAL.
newsitem.headline: AKBANK TO ADD 17 TRLN LIRA CAPITAL GAIN TO CAPITAL.

text.p: Akbank TAS, one of Turkey's leading banks said it would add 17.25 trillion lira ($115 million) of capital gains from sale of equity stakes in group and non-group firms to its capital.

The bank, whose 50 trillion lira capital is largely owned by Haci Omer Sabanci Holding AS, one of Turkey's leading industrial conglomerates, sold full or partial equity stakes in three group and four non-group firms earlier this year.
Among them was Akbank's stakes in Philips' three Turkish subsidiaries, sold for $5.6 million to Philips Electronics NV and Philips Lighting Holding BV on July 28.
Turkish firms and banks' capital gains are exempted from corporate tax if they are used to increase capital.
Details of Akbank's capital rise will be announced later, following a board decision. The capital gains will have no effect on the bank's profit and loss statement.
Akbank's first half net profits rose by 56 percent in US dollar terms to $321 million this year from $206 in the same 1996 period, the bank statement said.
It also said assets grew 21 percent and loans 67 percent in dollar terms in the first half compared to a year ago. Turkey's year-on-year consumer price inflation was 78 percent in June.

"The strong results confirm that the strategy implemented in increasing the effectiveness of its branch network and marketing channels, aided by high technology and competitive funding advantage support the increase in customer base and market share," Akbank vice-chairman Erol Sabanci said in the statement.
Akbank plans to spend $29.7 million for information technology and raise the number of its domestic branches to 501 from current 493 this year.
Its marketing moves include setting up 10 satellite branches, an additional marketing channel without operations to raise the total number to 14 this year.
